items.followUp: Write two characteristics of bus topology.

rubric.why: In a star topology, each device connects to a central device.
rubric.description: State that devices connect to a central hub, switch, or device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the central connection point.

rubric.why: Failure of the central device interrupts communication between connected devices.
rubric.description: State a distinct characteristic or consequence of star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the effect of central-device failure.

modelAnswer: Each computer or device is connected to a central hub or switch.
If the central hub fails, communication between the connected devices stops.

rubric.why: File sharing makes files available to other users or computers.
rubric.description: State that file sharing makes files available to others.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea of making files available.

rubric.why: Other users or computers can access or transfer the shared files.
rubric.description: Mention access to or transfer of files by other users or computers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct way others use shared files.

modelAnswer: File sharing is the process of making files available to other users or computers.
Users can access or transfer shared files, often over a network.

items.followUp: Write one valid example of an IPv4 address and state how many parts it has.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid IPv4 example.

rubric.why: IPv4 uses four decimal numbers separated by dots.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying four decimal numbers separated by dots.

modelAnswer: An example of an IPv4 address is 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: Name the four layers of the TCP/IP model and briefly state the function of each.

rubric.why: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both parts of the correct expansion.

rubric.why: The Application layer provides network services to applications and users.
rubric.description: Name the Application layer and state its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer name and a correct function.

rubric.why: The Transport layer manages end-to-end communication and data delivery.
rubric.description: Name the Transport layer and state its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer name and a correct function.

rubric.why: The Internet layer handles addressing and routing; the Network Access layer sends data over the physical network.
rubric.description: Name and describe the Internet and Network Access layers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both lower layers and their general functions.

modelAnswer: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol; it is a suite of protocols used for communication over networks.
The Application layer provides network services to applications and users.
The Transport layer manages end-to-end communication and delivery of data.
The Internet layer handles logical addressing and routing of packets between networks.
The Network Access layer sends and receives data over the physical network medium.

items.followUp: Write a short note on phishing and identity theft as cybercrimes.

rubric.why: Hacking involves gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or network.
rubric.description: Describe hacking as unauthorised access to a system or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing hacking.

rubric.why: A virus or malware attack uses harmful software to damage systems or data.
rubric.description: Describe a harmful virus or malware attack.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the attack and stating its harmful effect.

rubric.why: Phishing uses fake messages or websites to trick people into revealing sensitive information.
rubric.description: Describe phishing and how it obtains sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of phishing.

rubric.why: Cyberstalking uses the internet to harass someone, while identity theft uses another person's information to impersonate them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing either type of cybercrime.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or network.
A virus or malware attack uses harmful software to damage a computer or its data.
Phishing uses fake emails or websites to trick people into giving passwords or other personal information.
Cyberstalking is using the internet to harass or threaten a person; identity theft involves using another person’s personal information to impersonate them.
